Squat: Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out. Sit your hips back and down until thighs are about level with the floor, chest up and knees tracking over your toes, then drive up through your whole foot.
Back squat: Rest the bar on your upper back, grip just outside your shoulders and brace your stomach. Sit down between your heels until thighs are level with the floor, keep your chest up, then stand by pushing the floor away.
Goblet squat: Hold one dumbbell or kettlebell against your chest with both hands. Squat down between your knees with your elbows inside them, chest tall, then drive back up.
Band squat: Stand on the band and hold the ends at your shoulders. Squat down with your chest up and knees over your toes, then stand up tall against the band.
Jump squats: Squat down to about half depth, then jump straight up as high as you can. Land softly on the balls of your feet, sink straight into the next squat.
Bulgarian split squat: Stand a big step in front of a bench and rest the top of your back foot on it. Lower straight down until your front thigh is level, keeping your front knee over your foot, then push up through the front heel.
Pistol squat progression: Stand on one leg with the other leg out in front. Sit back slowly onto a box or bench behind you, then stand up on one leg. Lower the box over time as you get stronger.
Wall sit: Lean your back flat against a wall and slide down until your knees are bent to 90 degrees, knees over ankles. Hold still and keep breathing.
Leg press: Sit with your back flat on the pad and feet shoulder-width on the plate. Lower until knees reach about 90 degrees without your lower back lifting, then press back up without locking your knees hard.
Leg extension: Sit with the pad on your lower shins and knees lined up with the machine's pivot. Straighten your legs fully, squeeze your thighs for a second, then lower slowly.
Leg curl: Line your knees up with the machine's pivot and put the pad just above your heels. Curl your heels toward you as far as you can, then lower slowly.
Lunges: Step forward with one leg and lower until both knees are bent about 90 degrees, back knee just above the floor. Push through the front heel to come back, then switch legs.
Walking lunge: Step forward into a lunge, back knee just above the floor and chest tall. Push up and bring the back leg straight through into the next lunge, moving forward each step.
Reverse lunge: Step one foot back and lower until your back knee nearly touches the floor, front knee over your ankle. Push through the front heel to stand back up.
Dumbbell lunge: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Step forward and lower until both knees are about 90 degrees, then push back to standing and switch legs.
Lateral lunge: Take a big step out to the side and sit your hips back over that foot, keeping the other leg straight and both feet flat. Push off to return to the middle.
Lunge jumps: Start in a lunge. Jump up and switch legs in the air, landing softly in a lunge with the other leg in front. Keep your chest up.
Deadlift: Stand with the bar over your mid-foot, hinge down and grip just outside your legs. Brace, flatten your back, then stand up by pushing the floor away, keeping the bar close to your legs. Lower it the same way.
Romanian deadlift: Hold the weight in front of your thighs with soft knees. Push your hips back and slide the weight down your legs until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, back flat, then squeeze your glutes to stand up.
Dumbbell Romanian deadlift: Hold dumbbells in front of your thighs with soft knees. Push your hips back and lower the weights down your legs with a flat back until your hamstrings stretch, then drive your hips forward to stand.
Single-leg Romanian deadlift: Stand on one leg with a soft knee. Hinge forward, reaching your hands down as your other leg goes straight back, hips level, then return to standing.
Glute bridge: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat near your hips. Squeeze your glutes and lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to knees, pause, then lower.
Hip thrust: Rest your upper back on a bench with feet flat and the weight across your hips. Drive your hips up until your body is flat like a table, squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower.
Calf raise: Stand with the balls of your feet on a step, heels hanging off. Rise up as high as you can onto your toes, pause, then lower your heels below the step slowly.
Standing calf raise: Stand tall, feet hip-width. Rise onto the balls of your feet as high as you can, pause for a second, then lower slowly. Use a step for more range.
Band lateral walk: Put a band around your legs just above the knees. Get into a quarter squat and take small steps sideways, keeping tension on the band and your toes forward.
Single-leg balance: Stand on one foot with a soft knee and hips level. Hold still for the time, then switch. Close your eyes to make it harder.
Copenhagen plank: Lie on your side and rest your top leg on a bench, bottom leg underneath. Lift your hips so your body is straight, held up by your top leg and forearm. Bend the top knee to make it easier.
Push-ups: Hands a little wider than your shoulders, body straight from head to heels. Lower your chest to just above the floor with elbows at about 45 degrees, then push back up. Drop to your knees if needed.
Diamond push-up: Make a diamond shape with your thumbs and index fingers under your chest. Keep your body straight, lower your chest to your hands with elbows close to your sides, then push up.
Pike push-up: Start in a push-up position, then walk your feet in so your hips are high like an upside-down V. Bend your elbows to lower the top of your head toward the floor, then press back up.
Hindu push-ups: Start in a downward dog with hips high. Swoop your chest down close to the floor and forward between your hands, ending with your chest up and arms straight, then push your hips back up to start.
Scapular push-ups: Hold a push-up position with straight arms. Without bending your elbows, let your chest sink so your shoulder blades squeeze together, then push the floor away to spread them apart.
Bench press: Lie on the bench with eyes under the bar, feet flat, shoulder blades pinched together. Lower the bar to your mid-chest with elbows at about 45 degrees, then press it back up over your shoulders.
Dumbbell bench press: Lie on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand at chest level. Press them up until your arms are straight over your chest, then lower slowly until your elbows are just below the bench.
Incline dumbbell press: Set the bench to a low incline. Start with dumbbells at your upper chest and press them up and slightly together, then lower slowly.
Dumbbell floor press: Lie on the floor with knees bent and a dumbbell in each hand. Lower until your upper arms touch the floor, pause, then press straight up.
Chest press machine: Set the seat so the handles line up with your mid-chest. Press the handles forward until your arms are straight, then let them come back slowly without the weights touching.
Band chest press: Wrap the band behind your back and hold an end in each hand at chest height. Press your hands straight forward until your arms are straight, then return slowly.
Cable fly: Stand between the cables with a handle in each hand, a slight bend in your elbows. Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a hugging motion, then open back up slowly.
Overhead press: Hold the bar at your collarbones, hands just outside your shoulders. Squeeze your glutes and stomach, press the bar straight up past your face until your arms lock out overhead, then lower it.
Dumbbell shoulder press: Sit or stand with dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward. Press them straight up until your arms are straight, then lower to your shoulders.
Kettlebell press: Hold the kettlebell at your shoulder with the bell resting on your forearm. Brace and press it straight overhead, then lower it back to your shoulder.
Shoulder press machine: Set the seat so the handles start at shoulder height. Press up until your arms are straight, then lower slowly.
Lateral raise: Stand with dumbbells at your sides and a slight bend in your elbows. Raise your arms out to the sides up to shoulder height, then lower slowly. Use light weights.
Dips: Support yourself on parallel bars with straight arms. Lower until your upper arms are about level with the floor, leaning slightly forward, then push back up.
Triceps pushdown: Stand at the cable with elbows pinned to your sides. Push the bar or rope down until your arms are straight, then let it come back up to about chest height.
Triceps extension: Hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands. Keep your elbows pointing up and lower the weight behind your head, then straighten your arms.
Skull crushers: Lie on a bench holding the weight above your chest. Bend only at the elbows to lower it toward your forehead, then straighten your arms back up.
Cable kickback: Hinge forward slightly holding the cable with your elbow pinned to your side. Straighten your arm back behind you, squeeze, then return slowly.
Handstand wall hold: Place your hands about a hand's width from a wall and kick up so your heels rest on it. Push the floor away with straight arms and hold, keeping your stomach tight.
Pseudo planche lean: Get in a push-up position with your hands turned out and by your waist. Lean your shoulders forward past your hands with straight arms and hold.
Pull-ups: Hang from the bar with hands just wider than your shoulders, palms facing away. Pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows down, chin over the bar, then lower all the way down.
Chin-ups: Hang from the bar with palms facing you, hands shoulder-width. Pull up until your chin clears the bar, then lower slowly until your arms are straight.
Towel pull-ups: Hang two towels over a bar and grip one in each hand. Pull yourself up as high as you can, squeezing the towels hard, then lower slowly. Great for grip.
Lat pulldown: Sit with your thighs under the pad and grip the bar wider than your shoulders. Pull it down to your upper chest by driving your elbows down, then let it rise slowly.
Inverted row: Lie under a bar or table, grip it and hang with your body straight and heels on the floor. Pull your chest to the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades, then lower.
Bent-over row: Hinge forward with a flat back, holding the bar below your shoulders. Pull it to your lower ribs by driving your elbows back, then lower it slowly.
Dumbbell row: Put one hand and knee on a bench, back flat. Pull the dumbbell up to your hip with your elbow close to your side, then lower until your arm is straight.
Single-arm row: Brace one hand on a bench, back flat. Pull the weight up to your hip, squeezing your shoulder blade back, then lower it all the way.
Kettlebell row: Hinge forward with a flat back, kettlebell in one hand. Row it up to your hip, pause, then lower with control.
Seated cable row: Sit tall with knees slightly bent and grab the handle. Pull it to your belly button, squeezing your shoulder blades together, then let your arms straighten without rounding your back.
Seated row machine: Sit with your chest against the pad. Pull the handles back until your elbows are past your body, squeeze your shoulder blades, then return slowly.
Band row: Anchor the band at chest height. Hold the ends with straight arms, then pull your elbows back past your body and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Light band row: Anchor a light band at chest height and pull your elbows back, squeezing your shoulder blades. Move slowly and smoothly.
Face pull: Set the rope at face height. Pull it toward your forehead, splitting the rope apart and pulling your hands back by your ears, elbows high, then return slowly.
Band pull-apart: Hold a band in front of your chest with straight arms. Pull your hands apart until the band touches your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades, then return slowly.
Band external rotation: Hold a band with your elbow bent 90 degrees and pinned to your side. Rotate your forearm out away from your stomach, then return slowly.
Band internal rotation: Anchor a band to your side, elbow bent 90 degrees and pinned to your waist. Rotate your forearm in across your stomach, then return slowly.
Shoulder dislocates with band: Hold a band or stick wide in front of your hips. Keeping your arms straight, lift it up over your head and down behind you, then bring it back. Widen your grip if it hurts.
Barbell curl: Stand holding the bar with palms up, elbows at your sides. Curl it up to your shoulders without swinging, then lower slowly.
Dumbbell curl: Hold dumbbells at your sides with palms forward. Curl them up toward your shoulders keeping your elbows still, then lower slowly.
Hammer curl: Hold dumbbells at your sides with palms facing each other. Curl them up keeping that grip and your elbows still, then lower slowly.
Band curl: Stand on the band holding the ends with palms up. Curl your hands to your shoulders, elbows still, then lower slowly.
Farmer carry: Pick up a heavy weight in each hand. Stand tall with shoulders back and walk with short, steady steps without leaning to either side.
Plate pinch: Pinch two weight plates together, smooth sides out, between your fingers and thumb. Hold them at your side for the time.
Plank: Forearms on the floor under your shoulders, body straight from head to heels. Squeeze your glutes and stomach and don't let your hips sag or pike up. Breathe steadily.
Side plank: Lie on your side with your elbow under your shoulder. Lift your hips so your body is straight from head to feet and hold. Drop your bottom knee to make it easier.
Plank jacks: Hold a high plank on your hands. Jump your feet out wide and back together like a jumping jack, keeping your hips level.
Dead bug: Lie on your back with arms up and knees bent over your hips. Press your lower back into the floor, then slowly lower the opposite arm and leg toward the floor and return. Switch sides.
Bird dog: Start on hands and knees. Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are straight, keep your hips level, pause, then return and switch.
Crunch: Lie on your back with knees bent. Curl your shoulders up off the floor by squeezing your stomach, then lower slowly. Don't pull on your neck.
Bicycle crunch: Lie on your back with hands behind your head. Bring one knee in while turning the opposite elbow toward it, then switch sides in a slow pedaling motion.
Russian twist: Sit with knees bent and lean back slightly with a straight back. Rotate your chest and hands side to side, touching the floor beside each hip. Lift your feet to make it harder.
Leg raises: Lie on your back with legs straight and hands under your hips. Lift your legs up to vertical, then lower slowly without letting your lower back arch.
Hanging knee raise: Hang from a bar with straight arms. Lift your knees up toward your chest without swinging, then lower slowly.
Hanging leg raise: Hang from a bar and lift your straight legs up to hip height or higher, then lower slowly without swinging.
L-sit hold: Sit between two parallettes or on the floor with hands by your hips. Push down to lift your body and hold your legs straight out in front. Bend your knees to make it easier.
Pallof press: Stand side-on to a band or cable at chest height, holding it at your chest. Press your hands straight out and hold for a second without letting your body twist, then bring them back.
Superman: Lie face down with arms stretched forward. Lift your arms, chest and legs a few centimetres off the floor, squeeze your back, hold briefly, then lower.
Mountain climbers: Hold a high plank on your hands. Drive one knee toward your chest, then quickly switch legs as if running, keeping your hips low.
Flutter kicks: Lie on your back with hands under your hips. Lift your legs slightly and kick them up and down in small, quick movements, lower back pressed down.
Medicine ball rotational throw: Stand side-on to a wall holding the ball at your hip. Rotate from your hips and throw the ball hard into the wall, catch it, and repeat.
Medicine ball slam: Lift the ball overhead, rising onto your toes. Slam it down into the floor as hard as you can, bending at the hips, then pick it up and repeat.
Kettlebell swing: Stand with feet wide and the kettlebell in front of you. Hike it back between your legs, then snap your hips forward to swing it to chest height. Your hips do the work, not your arms.
Sandbag clean: Squat down and grab the bag. Pull it up your body explosively, catching it on your chest as you drop under it, then stand up tall.
Burpees: From standing, squat down and put your hands on the floor. Jump your feet back to a plank, do a push-up if you can, jump your feet back in and jump up with your arms overhead.
High knees: Run on the spot, driving each knee up to hip height and pumping your arms. Stay on the balls of your feet.
Jump rope: Hold the handles at hip height and turn the rope with your wrists. Make small, light jumps on the balls of your feet just high enough to clear the rope.
Box jumps: Stand in front of a sturdy box. Swing your arms and jump up, landing softly on the box with both feet in a quarter squat. Step down, don't jump down.
Broad jumps: Stand with feet hip-width. Swing your arms back, then jump forward as far as you can, landing softly with bent knees. Reset before the next one.
Tuck jumps: Jump straight up and pull your knees toward your chest, then land softly on the balls of your feet and go straight into the next jump.
Skater jumps: Leap sideways from one foot to the other like a speed skater, landing softly on one leg with the other leg behind you.
Single-leg hops: Hop forward or on the spot on one foot, landing softly with a bent knee. Keep your knee over your toes. Switch legs.
Line jumps: Jump side to side or forward and back over a line as fast as you can, staying light on the balls of your feet.
Bear crawls: On hands and feet with knees hovering just off the floor, crawl forward by moving opposite hand and foot together. Keep your back flat and hips low.
Shuttle runs: Sprint to a line, touch it, turn and sprint back. Stay low as you turn.
Suicide sprints: Sprint to the first line and back, then the second line and back, then the third and back, touching each line.
Short sprints: Sprint flat out for the short distance or time, then walk back to recover fully before the next one.
Interval sprints: Run hard for the work time, then walk or jog easily for the rest time. Repeat for the number of rounds.
Full-court sprints: Sprint from baseline to baseline as fast as you can, then rest before the next one.
Strides: Gradually speed up over about 80 to 100 metres to around 90 percent of your top speed, stay relaxed, then slow down. Walk back to recover.
Hill repeats: Run up a hill hard with short, quick steps, leaning slightly forward. Walk or jog back down to recover.
Lateral shuffles: In an athletic stance, knees bent, shuffle sideways without crossing your feet, staying low.
Defensive slides: Get low with feet wide and hands out. Push off the trailing foot to slide sideways without letting your feet cross or click together.
Ladder footwork: Run through an agility ladder (or lines on the floor) with quick, light steps, touching each box in the pattern. Speed comes from staying on your toes.
Split-step and shuffle: Do a small hop to land on both feet in an athletic stance as if reacting to a shot, then shuffle quickly to one side and back.
Approach footwork: Practise your run-up into the jump: the last two steps are quick and big, arms swing back then up as you jump. Land on both feet.
Walking: Walk at a brisk pace where you can still talk. Stand tall and let your arms swing.
Easy run: Run at a relaxed pace where you can speak in full sentences. Short, light steps, relaxed shoulders.
Long run: Run slowly and steadily for the whole time. If you can't talk in sentences, slow down.
Tempo run: After an easy warm-up, run at a comfortably hard pace you could hold for about an hour, then cool down.
Running: Run at a pace you can keep for the whole time, staying relaxed and breathing steadily.
Run/walk intervals: Alternate running easily for the run time and walking for the walk time. Keep the running gentle.
Interval repeats: Run the repeat hard but controlled, then jog or walk easily to recover before the next one.
Race-pace repeats: Run each repeat at the pace you want to hold in your race, with easy recovery jogs between.
Easy ride: Pedal at an easy effort where you can chat, with a light gear and smooth pedalling.
Easy cycling: Pedal at an easy effort where you can chat, with a light gear and smooth pedalling.
Steady ride: Ride at a moderate, steady effort you could hold for the whole time, breathing a little harder but in control.
Cycling warm-up: Pedal easily for a few minutes, gradually adding a little more effort.
Hard cycling intervals: Ride hard for the work time, then pedal easily to recover. Repeat.
Hard intervals: Go hard for the work time at an effort you can just hold, then recover easily before the next one.
Swimming: Swim at a steady pace with long strokes, breathing to the side every two or three strokes.
Easy swim: Swim slowly with relaxed, long strokes. Focus on breathing out underwater.
Cool-down swim: Swim slowly with any stroke to bring your breathing back down.
Freestyle laps: Swim front crawl with long strokes, rotating your body and breathing to the side. Keep your head down and kick from the hips.
Kick set with board: Hold a kickboard out in front and kick from your hips with nearly straight legs and pointed toes.
Kick drills: Kick from the hips with long legs and loose ankles, on your front, side or back.
Pull set: Put a pull buoy between your thighs so your legs float, and swim using only your arms.
Catch-up drill: Swim freestyle, but leave one arm stretched forward until the other arm comes all the way round to touch it.
Fingertip drag drill: Swim freestyle and drag your fingertips along the water's surface as your arm comes forward, to keep your elbow high.
Dive and recover: Practise diving low for the ball, rolling or sliding through, then getting back to your feet as quickly as you can.
Dribbling drills: Dribble the ball with your fingertips at waist height, eyes up, switching hands and speeds.
Dribbling drill: Dribble through cones or a set path with small touches, keeping the ball close and your eyes up when you can.
Stationary dribbling: Stand in an athletic stance and dribble hard with one hand, then the other, eyes up.
Cone dribbling: Dribble around a line of cones with small, quick touches using both feet or hands.
Crossover and between-the-legs: Dribble low and switch hands in front of your body (crossover), then through your legs, staying in a low stance.
Form shooting: Stand close to the basket. Elbow under the ball, shoot with one hand, the other hand just guiding, and follow through with your wrist.
Free throws: Same routine every time: feet set, a few dribbles, eyes on the rim, then a smooth shot with a full follow-through.
Mid-range shooting: Shoot from just inside the three-point line, catching in a ready stance and rising straight up.
Three-point shooting: Catch behind the line with knees bent, use your legs for power and keep the same shooting form.
Layup finishes: Drive in, take your last two steps, jump off the opposite foot to your shooting hand, and lay the ball softly off the backboard.
Passing drills: Pass to a partner or wall with a firm, accurate pass, stepping into it, and catch with soft hands.
Wall passing: Pass the ball against a wall with the inside of your foot and control the rebound, using both feet.
First touch and control: Receive the ball and cushion it with your first touch so it stops close to you, ready for the next move.
Juggling: Keep the ball in the air with small touches using your feet, thighs and head. Count your best streak.
Shadow swings: Practise your swing without a ball, slowly and with good form, then at normal speed.
Shadowboxing: Stay in your stance, light on your feet, and throw punch combinations into the air while moving and keeping your hands up.
Small-sided game: Play a short game with few players per side, staying active and touching the ball a lot.
Pickup game: Play a casual game at a steady effort, staying involved at both ends.
Stance and motion: Get in your wrestling stance: feet wide, knees bent, back flat, head up, hands in front. Move forward, back and sideways without crossing your feet or standing up.
Penetration steps: From your stance, drop your level and take a big step forward with your lead leg, landing on your back knee, then bring your back foot up and stand back into stance.
Double-leg shots: Drop your level, step in deep between your partner's feet, wrap both legs behind the knees with your head on their side, and drive through to finish.
Single-leg shots: Drop your level and step to one of your partner's legs, grab it behind the knee with both hands, head tight to their chest, and lift or run the pipe to finish.
Sprawls: From your stance, shoot your legs straight back and drop your hips to the floor, chest up and arms ready to block, then pop back up into stance.
Sprawl-and-shot drill: Sprawl, pop back up to stance, then immediately shoot a takedown. Keep alternating for the time.
Hand fighting: From your stance with a partner, fight for inside control of the hands and wrists, clearing their grips and getting your own.
Stand-ups: From bottom position, post your outside foot, drive your back up into your partner, clear their hands from your waist and turn to face them.
Sit-outs: From hands and knees, kick one leg through underneath you so you're sitting, then turn your chest back toward the mat. Switch sides.
Granby rolls: From your knees, drop one shoulder to the mat and roll over your shoulders and back onto your knees on the other side, keeping your neck safe.
Hip heists: From sitting with hands behind you, lift your hips, swing one leg through underneath you and come up onto your knee facing the other way.
Neck bridges: Lie on your back, plant your feet and roll your weight up onto the top of your head, with hands beside your head for support. Roll gently forward and back. Start very easy.
Neck isometrics: Press your hand against your forehead and push your head into it without moving, then do the back and both sides. Hold each push.
Neck circles: Slowly roll your head in a gentle circle, then the other way. Keep it slow and comfortable.
Live drilling: Wrestle with a partner at match speed from a set position, resetting after each score.
Spin drill: Partner on hands and knees. With your chest on their back, spin around them in a circle, staying heavy on their back. Switch directions.
Bridge and roll: Lie on your back, bridge your hips up onto your head and feet, then turn and roll over one shoulder onto your stomach.
Partner carries: Lift your partner onto your back or shoulders and walk with a tall chest and braced stomach.
Rope climb: Grip the rope high, pinch it between your feet, stand up on your feet, and reach higher. Climb down hand over hand.
Cat-cow: On hands and knees, round your back up toward the ceiling, then let it sink as you lift your chest and tailbone. Move slowly with your breath.
Downward dog: From hands and knees, lift your hips up and back into an upside-down V. Press your heels toward the floor and lengthen your back.
Child's pose: Kneel, sit back onto your heels and fold forward with arms stretched in front. Relax and breathe into your back.
World's greatest stretch: Step into a deep lunge, put the same-side hand down inside your front foot, then rotate and reach your other arm to the ceiling. Return and switch.
Hip flexor stretch: Kneel on one knee with the other foot in front. Squeeze the glute of the back leg and shift your hips forward until you feel a stretch in the front of the hip.
Hamstring stretch: Sit or stand with one leg straight. Hinge forward from your hips with a flat back until you feel a stretch behind your thigh.
Pigeon pose: From hands and knees, bring one knee forward behind your wrist with the shin angled across, and stretch the other leg straight back. Lower your hips and breathe.
Hip 90/90: Sit with both knees bent to 90 degrees, one leg in front and one to the side. Sit tall, then rotate your knees over to the other side without using your hands if you can.
Thoracic rotation: On hands and knees, put one hand behind your head and rotate that elbow up toward the ceiling, following it with your eyes, then down under your body.
Thoracic rotations: On hands and knees, put one hand behind your head and rotate that elbow up toward the ceiling, following it with your eyes, then down under your body.
Breathing drill: Lie or sit comfortably. Breathe in slowly through your nose for about four seconds, filling your belly, then breathe out slowly for six seconds.
Shrimping: Lie on your back, plant one foot, push your hips away to the side and slide your body back, then switch sides and repeat down the mat.
Upa bridges: Lie on your back with feet planted near your hips, drive your hips high and turn over one shoulder, then come back down and switch sides.
Technical stand-up: Sit with one hand behind you and the other arm up to guard your face, lift your hips, swing your back leg through and stand up into your stance.
Forward shoulder rolls: From kneeling, tuck your head to the side, roll diagonally over one shoulder to the opposite hip and come up onto your knee.
Backward shoulder rolls: From sitting, roll back and turn your head to one side, roll over that shoulder (not your neck) and come up onto your knees.
Breakfalls: Sit or squat low, roll back with your chin tucked and slap the mat hard with both arms at about 45 degrees to soften the fall.
Guard retention drill: Lie on your back with feet up like you are in guard and keep turning your hips and legs to face an imaginary partner circling you.
Inverted guard drill: From your back, lift your hips, roll up onto your shoulders and turn your legs around overhead to face the other way, then come back.
Hip bump sweeps: Sit up on one hand, drive your hips up and forward, and reach your other arm over as if bumping a partner over your shoulder.
Armbar drill: On your back, swing one leg over as if across a partner's face, pivot your hips to the side and squeeze your knees together. Switch sides.
Triangle drill: On your back, shoot your hips up, swing one leg over your shoulder line and lock the other leg over your ankle, squeezing your knees.
Guard passing footwork: Stay low with a wide base and step quickly side to side around an imaginary guard, keeping your hips heavy and your hands in front.
Knee-on-belly switches: Kneel with one knee on a pad or mat as if on a partner's belly, then hop and switch knees, keeping your weight on the knee and your base wide.
Sprawl and go-behind: Sprawl your legs back and drop your hips, then walk your feet around to one side as if taking your partner's back. Switch sides.
Gi grip hangs: Hang from a bar using a towel or gi draped over it, squeezing the cloth hard, with your shoulders set down away from your ears.
Gi pull-ups: Hang a towel or gi over a pull-up bar, grip the cloth and pull your chest up toward your hands, then lower slowly.
Turkish get-up: Lie down holding a kettlebell straight up, then stand up step by step while keeping it locked overhead, and reverse it to lie back down.
Live rolling: Spar with a partner at a steady pace. Tap early to any submission and let go as soon as your partner taps.
Positional sparring: Start from one position, like guard or side control, and spar until someone sweeps, passes or taps, then reset.
Hollow hold: Lie on your back, press your low back into the floor and lift your shoulders and straight legs a few inches off the ground. Hold.
